prayerJournal.example: Keep this request in your prayer journal.
prayerJournal.note: The nav tab may say “Journal”; sentences say “prayer journal” when the context is not already clear.

update.example: Add an update when something changes.
update.note: News on a prayer request. App software updates are a different, technical word.

thanksgiving.example: End with thanksgiving for what God has done.
thanksgiving.note: The prayer stage of thanking God; “gratitude” for the feeling.

renunciation.example: A prayer of renunciation names what you turn away from.
renunciation.note: Deliverance vocabulary: a spoken turning away in Christ’s name, not self-denial in general.

sanctification.example: Sanctification is God's work in us.
sanctification.note: God's work of making believers holy over time; never self-improvement or self-optimisation.

calling.note: God's call on a life; not career branding or 'purpose' coaching.

surrender.example: Surrender to God is trust, not resignation.
surrender.note: Entrusting oneself and one's desires to God's will (Gethsemane); not resignation, defeat or passivity.

abidingInChrist.example: Abide in Christ as a branch in the vine.
abidingInChrist.note: John 15: remaining joined to Christ in trust and obedience, as a branch to the vine.

worship.example: Worship begins by looking to God.
worship.note: Honouring God for who He is; praise is one expression of worship.

confession.example: Confession opens the way to forgiveness.
confession.note: Telling God the truth about sin (1 John 1:9); distinct from a confession of faith.

forgiveness.note: God's forgiveness of sin, and forgiving others; forgiving never requires returning to danger.

prayer.note: Speaking with God; never a meditation technique or positive thinking.
